plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and is celebrated in art, poetry, and festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea, and cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms herald the end of winter in Japan, and ume viewing (kobai) traditionally precedes cherry blossom viewing by several weeks.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler petals. It naturalizes in woodlands and meadows and is one of the earliest spring bulbs in temperate Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used for early-stage Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A large Himalayan tree that bears enormous, goblet-shaped flowers on leafless branches. Individual blooms can reach 25 cm across, creating a spectacular display in late winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, evolving before bees existed, so their flowers are sturdy enough to be pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers held on tall, slender stems above strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere, it is still in bloom at the end of summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (December to March)
plants.location: South Africa; widely grown in Australia, New Zealand, and Mediterranean climates
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily, and its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
